title: The SBE-BEAM Operator Multisig hard-codes a three-party split so no single Sky body can execute parameter changes alone
content:
A.3.5.2.4.5.1.2 and A.3.5.2.4.5.1.3 specify the Operator of the SBE-BEAM as a multisig with a 4/6 signing requirement whose signers are two addresses controlled by the Core Facilitator, two by Core GovOps, and two by Operational GovOps Soter Labs.

The arithmetic is the point. With three parties holding two keys each, no single party's two signatures reach the threshold of four, and no single party can block a transaction the other two support (four signatures are available from any two parties). The threshold enforces cross-party cooperation without letting any one party veto.

A.3.5.2.4.5.1.5 turns that arrangement into an invariant rather than a snapshot: signers may change the signer set themselves, but only so long as there are exactly six signers, exactly four are required, and the two-two-two split across those same three bodies is retained. Key rotation is permitted; recomposition is not.

This is what makes the SBE-BEAM's bypass of Governance Polls tolerable. The bounds in A.3.5.2.4 limit *what* can be done; this structure limits *who* can do it, and does so in a way the operators cannot quietly renegotiate from inside the multisig.
description: Four-of-six signing with two signers each from the Core Facilitator, Core GovOps and Operational GovOps Soter Labs; signers may rotate only if that exact composition is preserved.
